narrative: During overhaul of pump P-204 the suction valve was closed but not locked or tagged, and the fitter broke the flange while residual pressure was still trapped in the line. Product sprayed across the bund. Nobody was standing in front of the joint.

Scaffold plank at the 8 metre lift moved underfoot as a fitter stepped onto it. His harness lanyard was clipped to the handrail rather than to the anchor point. He recovered his balance without falling.

Two technicians entered crude tank T-12 through the side manway to inspect the floor. The gas test had been done the previous evening and no fresh reading was taken before entry. No hole watch was posted.
Crane operator continued slewing a 4.2 tonne casing bundle after losing sight of the banksman for roughly three minutes. Two roustabouts were working under the swing path at the pipe rack.
Welder started cutting on the produced water line at GGS-3 on a permit that had been raised for the adjacent skid. The area gas test was not repeated after the line was opened.
H2S alarm at the wellhead sounded at 42 ppm while two technicians were changing a gauge. Neither man was carrying a personal monitor and the nearest SCBA set was in the vehicle 200 metres upwind.

Light vehicle returning from the rig at night crossed the centre line on the Duliajan-Naharkatiya road and left the carriageway. Driver reported he had been on duty for fourteen hours. No collision occurred.
Fitter bypassed the interlock on the compressor discharge so the unit would keep running through the shift. The bypass was not recorded and was found by the next shift supervisor during handover.
Crew began breaking the flange on the test separator line before the permit to work had come back signed. Work was stopped by the area authority within about ten minutes.
Electrician opened the 415 V panel to replace a contactor and found the isolator had been racked back in by another crew. He was wearing gloves but no arc flash protection.

Drill crew were tripping out when the elevator latch was found not to be fully engaged. The stand was set back without incident. Latch had been reported sticky on the previous tour and not attended to.
A joint of tubing rolled off the pipe rack as the strop was slackened. Two men were standing on the low side of the rack. The joint stopped against the rack leg.
Hydrogen sulphide detector at the separator skid was found taped over with polythene, apparently to stop it alarming during purging. Detector had been in that condition for an unknown period.
Contractor erected mobile scaffold on soft ground beside the ETP tank without base plates or outrigger legs. Two men were working from the top deck at approximately 4 metres when it was noticed.
Excavator bucket swung within about a metre of a survey team member who had walked into the exclusion zone to take a photograph. No barrier tape had been run on the approach side.
During the nitrogen purge of the flare header the vent was found discharging at grade rather than at height. Two operators reported light-headedness and moved upwind. Both recovered fully.
Rigger climbed the derrick to free a snagged air hose without a fall arrest system and without informing the driller. He came down when instructed.
Forklift carrying a drum pallet reversed across the warehouse door while a storeman was walking through. The reversing alarm was not working. Both stopped short.
Grinding sparks from fabrication work landed inside an open drain that runs to the oily water sump. No fire blanket was in place and the drain had not been covered as the permit required.
Operator opened a sample point on the LPG line wearing cotton gloves and no face shield. A small liquid release occurred and flashed off. No contact with skin.
Pressure gauge on the wellhead was found reading 0 while the annulus was known to be live. Gauge isolation valve had been left shut. Crew were about to work on the basis of that reading.
Night shift found the emergency shutdown push button at the compressor house obstructed by a stack of empty drums. ESD had not been tested since the last turnaround.
Slip on the stairway from the pump house landing. Handrail is in place and the step was wet from rain. Minor bruising to forearm. First aid given on site.
Approximately five litres of hydraulic oil leaked from a burst hose on the workover unit. Fully contained within the drip tray and cleaned up. Hose was at the end of its service life.
Housekeeping observation: welding cables and airlines run across the walkway between the workshop bays, creating a trip hazard. Rerouted the same day.
Storeman reported back discomfort after manually lifting a 25 kg valve box from a low shelf without assistance. Advised on team lifting and referred to the medical centre.
Two of six eyewash stations in the process area were found with the water flow restricted and the inspection tags out of date. Flushed and retagged.
Perimeter lighting at the Kusijan gas gathering station was out on the north fence line for the second consecutive night, leaving the walkway to the control room unlit.
Contract painter observed without safety goggles while preparing a surface with a wire brush. Stopped, goggles issued, task resumed.
Toolbox talk record for the day shift was found unsigned by three crew members who were on the job. Supervisor completed the briefing and the record retrospectively.
Minor crude seepage noticed at the flange of the group gathering station header. Estimated less than two litres, contained inside the bund, tightened and monitored.
Printer in the field office ran out of toner during shift handover and the paper log had to be written by hand. Reported to administration.
